This was to be done through the development of a detailed DER control strategy, supporting integrations, operational requirements, and integration designs to enable peak load management, frequency support and contingency reserves. The specific supporting subtasks include: - Subtask 1.1.0: Develop DER control strategy - Subtask 1.2.0: Compile inventory of DERs and schedule for advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) installation - Subtask 1.3.0: Model distribution grid needs - Subtask 1.4.0: Design architecture and communication pathways There were several actions taken to develop and define the grid services including: (1) development of control parameters; (2) automation definition; (3) telecommunication and integration requirements; (4) development and testing in the test environment of the EMS with the Open Systems International, Inc (OSI) Monarch and Integra Distributed Energy Resource Management System (DERMS) solution; and (5) DER definition and configuration requirements within the software. 6 6.1.1.1 Subtask 1.1.0: Develop DER Control Strategy Grid Services Definition. The EMS support team worked to define parameters for frequency response control such that thresholds for frequency could be set that would automatically trigger a frequency response event through the EMS system if the frequency went above or below the defined allowable operating band over a certain period of time. A calculation was developed to detect frequency events with the goal of catching most of the events that fall under the BAL-003 reliability standards as defined by the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC). The speed at which frequency response events must occur dictated the telecommunication and integration requirements for the DERs and further played a role with DER eligibility for this grid service. While the initial grid services definition was focused on establishing requirements for the frequency support grid service, PacifiCorp and the project team further defined the grid services through a series of grid services workshops. The workshop meetings have covered the expected event response time, the duration of the event, types of DERs most pertinent to each grid service, any telemetry and control signal requirements, and event notification
